faq.q: What time should a New Year’s Eve party start?
faq.a: Start at 8 or 9 p.m. Four hours before midnight gives you time for two rounds of food, a couple of games and a real build to the countdown without anyone flagging by 11. If your crowd runs late, 9 p.m. works. For guests who want to leave early, toast midnight in another time zone around 10 p.m.

faq.q: What do adults do on New Year’s Eve at home?
faq.a: Pick a theme like decades, black and gold or pajamas, serve food in two waves plus a midnight snack, and play one game an hour: resolution guessing, year-in-review trivia or fishbowl. Build up to a synced countdown with confetti or a balloon drop and a toast, then dance, eat fries and get everyone home safely.

faq.q: How much champagne do I need for a New Year’s Eve party?
faq.a: For the midnight toast alone, one 750 ml bottle pours about six 4-ounce glasses, so divide your guest count by six and round up: four bottles for 20 people. If you’re serving sparkling wine all night, a bottle pours about five standard 5-ounce glasses. Add zero-proof bubbles for anyone not drinking.

faq.q: How do you do a balloon drop at home?
faq.a: Hang a plastic tablecloth like a hammock from two ceiling hooks or a curtain rod, fill it with inflated balloons, and tie a string to one edge. At midnight, pull the string to tip the balloons onto the crowd. Test it a few hours before the party so the only surprise is the good kind.

faq.q: How can you celebrate New Year’s Eve if you can’t stay up until midnight?
faq.a: Celebrate someone else’s midnight. On Eastern time, London rings in the new year at 7 p.m. and Rio de Janeiro and Buenos Aires at 10 p.m. On Pacific time, New York’s midnight arrives at 9 p.m. Do the countdown, the toast and the confetti then, and you’re in bed before the neighbors start.
